title: Resolve sparse-whitespace & zero-width tokenization mismatches for chat template pinning during model onboarding
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: During onboarding for several new model variants we observed downstream chat template mismatches caused by sparse or nonstandard whitespace characters (non-breaking spaces, zero-width joiners, and mixed Unicode separators). When pinning a specific model version, these tokenizer differences lead to subtle role delimiter misalignment which breaks structured output parsers and causes noisy eval regressions.

Goal: Implement a lightweight normalization/heuristic layer in the onboarding pipeline that: (1) detects and harmonizes sparse-whitespace edgecases in tokenizer outputs, (2) applies conservative role-delimiter canonicalization for chat templates only at onboarding time (without changing runtime model tokenization), and (3) republishes a validated performance/latency profile tied to the pinned model version.

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarding pipeline normalizes non-breaking spaces, NBSP variants, and common zero-width characters before comparing token boundaries against chat template role delimiters.
- A heuristic toggle allows preserving whitespace semantics for customers who opt-out; default is safe normalization.
- End-to-end onboarding tests show no template alignment regressions across the pinned model matrix (validated on 5 representative models and short/long sequence inputs).
- Performance profile publish job runs as part of the final onboarding step and attaches the normalization flag to the published profile metadata.
- Documentation and release notes updated; console shows the normalization flag on model detail pages.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Triage: Sofia reproduced mismatch with model-variant gptx-1.1-fc. Template role tokens (<<assistant>>/<<user>>) split across tokens when input contains NBSP and ZWJ sequences. Repro script added to onboarding-tests repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-tests/pull/72

2026-03-01 - Design sync: Opted for a non-invasive approach: perform normalization in the onboarding pre-checker rather than modifying tokenizer configs. Rationale: avoids runtime divergence for existing customers. Decision log updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenization+Edgecases+Decision

2026-03-03 - Implementation: Added normalizer module 'sparse_ws_normalizer' to onboarding service. Initial implementation strips and maps NBSP (U+00A0), narrow no-break space (U+202F), zero-width joiner (U+200D) to tidy placeholders before token-boundary checks. Unit tests added (local run: 124 tests, 4 failures unrelated). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/198

2026-03-06 - Perf check: End-to-end onboarding smoke with pinned model matrix (5 models) ran in CI. Median onboarding time increased +0.9% due to normalization step (within perf SLO). Added caching for repeated inputs to mitigate cost. Benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/onboard/edgecases

2026-03-09 - Review feedback (Marina K.): Please add explicit handling for mixed-directional whitespace (RTL markers) and include an opt-out flag surfaced in Console. Also add an integration test that exercises function-calling structured outputs. Filed follow-up subtasks: ENG-40145 (RTL handling), ENG-40146 (console opt-out UI).

2026-03-11 - QA: Ran regression suite against top 50 prompt templates used by customers. Found 2 failing templates where role delimiter canonicalization caused expected whitespace-sensitive outputs to change. Adjusted heuristic to only canonicalize role delimiters when they appear adjacent to normalized-space sequences. QA re-run passed. Test report uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1abcOnboardQA

2026-03-12 - Ready for merge: Addressed code review comments, added feature flag 'onboard.normalize_sparse_ws' (default=true). Added acceptance gating in pipeline to attach metadata 'normalization=on' to published performance profile. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/214 - awaiting infra-approve and runtime-1.20 cut.
implementation_notes: Normalization is only applied during onboarding pre-checks and token-boundary comparisons; we do not rewrite model tokenizer vocab or runtime tokenization to avoid customer-visible behavior changes.
Added small LRU cache keyed by input fingerprint to avoid repeated Unicode normalization overhead for high-frequency templates during batch onboarding runs.
Profile publisher now expects a 'normalization' tag and will include it in the published JSON at /profiles/{model}:{version}.json
Edgecases: preserved exact whitespace for inputs explicitly marked with 'preserve_whitespace:true' in onboarding manifest. This supports customers who rely on granular whitespace semantics.
qa_steps: Execute end-to-end onboarding on stage with pinned versions for models: gptx-1.1-fc, gptx-1.2-q8, redwood-neo-3b, open-llama-7b, community-4k; verify console shows normalization flag and profile published.
Run templated structured-output evals with function-calling enabled to validate role delimiter preservation.
Smoke-check latency on publication job: ensure publish latency delta < 2s per profile on stage infra.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: modifying runtime tokenizer would fix more cases but risks changing customer behavior and breaking cache/token-count based billing. Chosen onboarding-only normalization reduces blast radius.

Potential follow-up: build a tokenizer-compatibility test harness to detect these classes before onboarding so model teams can upstream fixes to tokenizers. See RFC: https://go.redwood.ai/rfc/tokenizer-compat-harness
